text: 53-year-old male. The patient was brought to the emergency department after an episode of loss of consciousness that occurred 1 hour ago, immediately after micturating. His wife found him unconscious on the bathroom floor. He regained consciousness after about 30 seconds without any confusion or amnesia for the event. No history of urinary incontinence during the event.

speaker: Doctor

The loss of consciousness occurring immediately after urination is highly suggestive of micturition syncope; have you experienced any dizziness, lightheadedness, or palpitations just before you passed out? Also, do you have a history of heart conditions or fainting spells before this incident?

The recent normal readings from your cardiac markers and other tests help rule out an acute cardiac event like a heart attack. However, the loss of consciousness immediately after urination without warning symptoms is still concerning. Do you have a history of seizures or fainting episodes unrelated to urination, and were you standing or sitting when this occurred?

text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Micturition Syncope. The loss of consciousness immediately following urination, with a rapid return to baseline and a normal cardiac workup, is diagnostic of this benign vasovagal event caused by vagal stimulation and pooling of blood in the perineal veins.
